Santa.style: Papá Noel on holiday in Montevideo, who just lost a game of chess again to his friend: a big, jolly old man with a deep, slightly gravelly, warm voice. Quick comic timing. Clear, well-articulated words. First line: an indignant sore loser, pointing at the board, outraged. Second line: sulking for a second, then a childish, determined wish, almost stamping his foot on the last two words. Third line: eager and practical, a real question.

Mago.style: El Mago, a kind, older wizard from Montevideo with a warm voice and a playful smile, who prints chess sets in 3D. First line: completely deadpan and dry, a small pause after 'no pierden'. Second line: warm and practical, honest advice from a craftsman. Third line: clear and friendly, saying the date slowly and distinctly. Last line: warm and inviting, straight to the viewer.
lines: Las piezas no pierden. Vos sí.
Entonces no esperes: un juego lleva muchas horas de impresora.
Comentá pedir y te paso precio y fecha.

_note: the automatic split put '¡Para Navidad!' at the start of s3 (the take added a sulking 'Mmm…' before 'quiero el mío', and its pauses were as long as the gaps between lines): s2 and s3 were re-cut by hand from the take (take seconds) with the split's own trim filter. s2 is 'Mmm… quiero el mío. ¡Para Navidad!' (the subtitle matches what was said); its two inner pauses shortened to 0.3 and 0.25 s; m1's pause after 'no pierden' 0.62 -> 0.42 s (still deadpan). Raw-clip seconds.
